participantInstructions: This is a team decision making event for two participants. The event is presented to you through your reading of the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation. You will have up to 30 minutes to review the case study, analyze the facts, and prepare your recommendation. You will then have up to 15 minutes to present your recommendation to the judge and respond to the judge's questions. Both members of your team must participate in the presentation and in answering the questions. You will be evaluated on how well you meet the performance indicators for this event. All of your notes and materials must be turned in at the end of the event.
situation:
You are the director of marketing and the director of supplier relations at LARKWOOD MARKETPLACE, an online platform that connects independent artisans with buyers of handmade home goods. The founder and chief executive officer (judge) built the company from a single online shop into a marketplace that now serves thousands of makers worldwide. After two years of declining sales, the CEO (judge) brought in a new leadership team last year and has asked your team to resolve a supplier issue before the holiday season begins.

LARKWOOD's best-selling category is hand-loomed textiles, nearly a third of which comes from THISTLEDOWN WEAVERS, an overseas workshop under contract since the marketplace was founded. THISTLEDOWN's patterns are licensed exclusively to LARKWOOD, an arrangement that keeps rival marketplaces from carrying identical designs. That exclusivity, together with reliable volume, has helped the textile category anchor the turnaround the new leadership team has pursued since taking over after two unprofitable years.

Last month, an independent labor-monitoring group published a report alleging that THISTLEDOWN requires seamstresses to work far beyond their scheduled shifts without additional pay, and that several workers were dismissed after raising safety concerns. THISTLEDOWN disputes the findings and has offered to let LARKWOOD send its own inspector before any decision is made. A second workshop, COLDBROOK FIBERS, sews comparable textiles under conditions that passed a recent independent audit and would welcome LARKWOOD's business, though it does not hold rights to THISTLEDOWN's exclusive patterns.

COLDBROOK can currently produce only about sixty percent of the volume THISTLEDOWN ships each month, and would need several months to expand further. Ending the THISTLEDOWN contract today would mean LARKWOOD cannot fill every textile order it currently promises, forcing a choice about which existing customers get priority while the shortfall lasts. Keeping the THISTLEDOWN contract in place while its inspection is arranged would preserve full supply, but it would mean continuing to sell products made under conditions a credible outside group has already questioned.

The CEO (judge) wants a clear recommendation on the THISTLEDOWN relationship: whether to keep it, suspend it pending inspection, or end it in favor of COLDBROOK. The recommendation should address how LARKWOOD would manage its textile supply and its customer commitments during any transition, and what the company should communicate, to whom, and on what timeline, once a direction is chosen.

The CEO (judge) will greet you in the boardroom and ask you to share your recommendation for the THISTLEDOWN contract and the resulting textile supply question. Be ready to explain why you chose that direction over the alternatives you considered along the way. After you present your analysis and answer the judge's questions, the CEO (judge) will thank you for your time and for the work your team put into this recommendation.
